what_happened.line: Members began ranking a rolled-up list of roughly two dozen FY27 capital requests, due to the chair by end of day the following Tuesday.
The town manager said the free cash figure needed to fund the capital plan will not even be estimated until January, clouding the timeline before town meeting.
The committee dropped the public safety garage heater request from the list because no cost estimate was ever submitted.
IT presented its only FY27 capital request, a network upgrade for the Adult Activity Center (Eagle House), alongside a longer-range five-year network plan carried in the operating budget instead.
The chair will have department heads and the town manager validate the rollup spreadsheet's figures before it goes back out to members.

why_it_matters: This rolled-up list is the slate of capital projects -- from a bridge repair to town network equipment to vehicles -- that will compete for funding recommendations going to town meeting, so how members rank them shapes what advances.

Not knowing the free cash figure until January means the committee may have to set priorities before it knows how much money is actually available, which could force re-ranking or cuts closer to town meeting.
A resident with a stake in a specific item, like the dropped heater request or the bridge project, should check whether it stays on the validated list once it comes back from department heads.
